answer.rationale: Finance mandates an 18% cut to component spend. The low-cost vendor's quote already meets the mandate alone, and memory_c2 documents that moving primary supply to this same vendor last year delivered sharp unit-cost reduction with quick onboarding and accurate invoicing—i.e., the transition risk is empirically low. The alternative of renewing the incumbent (memory_c1) preserves integration stability but does not meet the 18% reduction target without a renegotiation cycle we cannot fit into 14 days. Delivery-risk mitigation: the assembly line is at 94% of committed volume with no buffer, so the switch is viable precisely because current volume headroom absorbs any minor onboarding friction, and memory_c2 confirms onboarding was quick. I pull memory_c2 to confirm the low-cost vendor's operational record and memory_c1 to confirm the incumbent integration cost we are walking away from, ensuring the switch does not introduce a hidden migration expense that erodes the TCO saving. One decision, one cycle: switch primary vendor to the low-cost supplier effective at contract expiry.
